newsitem.title: MEXICO: Televisa Q2 seen improving marginally.
newsitem.headline: Televisa Q2 seen improving marginally.

text.p: Mexican media firm Grupo Televisa SA is expected to report slightly stronger operating earnings during the second quarter compared to the same period last year due to a pick-up in advertising revenues.
Three analysts interviewed by Reuters forecast quarterly operating profits of 324 million pesos versus 84 million pesos during the second quarter of last year, in constant pesos.

On a net profit level, however, the company was seen reporting a slight loss of 0.60 pesos per CPO ordinary share, not including extraordinary gains from the sale of Televisa's stake in PanAmSat Corp.

Including extraordinary items from the sale of PanAmSat, Televisa's quarterly profit per share was forecast at 12.55 pesos. That compares to an adjusted net gain of about 0.91 pesos per share during last year's second quarter.

On an operating level, analysts said the company's picture is improving slowly from the worst of the 1995-96 recession. Political advertising from July 6 mid-term elections also likely boosted revenues during the quarter, analysts said.
"There was quite a bit of new advertising from the political parties," said Shayne McGuire, an analyst at Deutche Morgan Grenfell in Mexico City.
McGuire said he expects television advertising to account for 26 percent of total revenues this quarter, compared to about 23 percent in most quarters.

Martin Lara, an analyst at Caspian Research in Mexico City, said the company's bottom line would be hurt by restructuring charges that are part of Televisa's three-year cost-cutting plan unveiled in May.
"The company's performance on an operating level is slowly improving, although these charges could hurt somewhat," Lara said.
The company has said it plans to take $80 million in restructuring charges this year, and much of that could come during the second quarter.

Analysts said they will keep a sharp eye on whether or not Televisa has continued to lose market share to rival TV Azteca. Azteca recently claimed it had more viewers during Mexico's July 6 election night than Televisa. A table comparing analysts
